newsitem.title: USA: Calif. adds 55,000 high-tech jobs in 1996-report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. adds 55,000 high-tech jobs in 1996-report.

text.p: California's high-tech firms created 55,000 jobs in 1996, accounting for nearly one-quarter of the nation's high-tech job growth, according to a report issued Monday.
Total high-tech employment in California topped 724,000 in 1996, its highest level of the decade, the American Electronics Association said in its Cyberstates report.

All of the major segments within California's high-tech industry experienced a boost in job growth in 1996. California's high-tech manufacturing sector added 28,400 new jobs last year, the association said.
Of the 26,200 new software and computer-related services jobs generated in 1996, the largest increases were in computer programming and prepackaged software, the association said.
The American Electronics Association is the nation's largest high-tech trade association.
